commentary:
Markets open the week risk-off ahead of a stacked macro calendar: Nasdaq futures are down 0.6% with tech leading global equities lower — an Alibaba $10.2bn share placement to fund AI capex added to jitters around the AI trade — as traders brace for PCE inflation data, Nvidia earnings and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole debut, where the stakes are elevated by simmering bond-market anxiety over debt supply and term premium. That anxiety has the dollar pinned near multi-month lows, and the overnight oil dip is offering relief to Treasuries, with the long bond and ultras bid while the front end sits still.

Energy is the day's talking point, and the direction is counterintuitive: despite Iran threatening 46 ships in a Strait of Hormuz transit crackdown, Brent is off 1.4% to $93 and WTI down 1.9%, with products hit harder still, as reports show the UAE, Iraq, Kuwait and now Saudi Arabia keeping barrels flowing across the waterway even as the war drags on — the supply-disruption premium is deflating. Watch Treasury Secretary Bessent's Iran press conference today for the next catalyst. European TTF gas bucked the move, up 2.5%, with carbon following.

Elsewhere, grains are firm — corn up 2.7%, wheat 1.9% — while arabica coffee extended its record run on the US-Colombia tariff spat, and sugar and cocoa gave back ground. Iron ore's 2.3% pop tracks China's $119bn policy-financing tool moving to project applications. CAD is the FX laggard, off 0.6%, as Ottawa signals little chance of trade talks resuming before the US midterms. Into Warsh and PCE, expect curve steepeners and the dollar to stay the pressure points.
